summary: Frontend-only UX validation for the SELTRACK WebUSB 'Access denied' troubleshoot fix. All 10 requested checks in the Devices/Settings dialog PASSED. The <details data-testid='usb-troubleshoot'> panel exists, is initially collapsed, expands on click, and contains every required string. The Web Serial button shows 'Recommended', WebUSB shows 'Advanced'. Clicking WebUSB with no device produces a user-facing 'No device selected.' toast (no uncaught exception), which validates the improved connectUSB() error-mapping path. Test Drawer Pulse is correctly disabled when not connected, and the Danger Zone reset button remains present.
critical_code_review_comments: printer.js connectUSB() correctly wraps usbDevice.open() in try/catch and maps 'Access denied' / claim errors to OS-specific hints (Windows/macOS/Linux) with actionable guidance and a Web Serial fallback.

Partial-open cleanup path (line 126) attempts usbDevice.close() before rethrowing — good, prevents leaking handles. Minor: NotFoundError branch is only checked at requestDevice(); the try/open block's regex correctly avoids catching NotFoundError since it wouldn't reach open().
SettingsDialog.jsx troubleshoot copy is comprehensive and matches the runtime error hint; keeps a single source of truth for both the toast (from printer.js) and the panel.
test_credentials: N/A - no auth required for this UI-only test
context_for_next_testing_agent: This iteration only verified the UI/UX of the WebUSB troubleshoot panel. Physical USB / Serial device flows still cannot be exercised in headless Playwright — those must be validated manually on a workstation with a thermal printer attached. All test-ids used: settings-btn, settings-dialog, connect-serial, connect-usb, usb-troubleshoot, test-drawer, reset-data-btn.
